original.target_description: Study 1 partial correlations of mean FY 2004–2006 company profits with power composite or global leadership ratings, controlling for attractiveness, affective expression, and age. Description names both predictors; correspondence to a single test is unresolved.

n.sample_role: CEO/company observations; ratings averaged across participants for each CEO. Final analytic N is not explicitly printed.
n.exclusions: One female CEO excluded from targets; two companies acquired in FY 2006 excluded from analysis; one CEO removed as an outlier. Three raters recognizing CEOs were removed, a separate contributor role.
n.location: pp. 109–110, Stimuli, footnote 1, Procedure, Results and Discussion; Table 1
n.quote: Trait and leadership ratings were averaged across participants ... for each CEO. Data for one CEO were removed from analysis ... because his score was more than 3 standard deviations below the ... mean for all CEOs.

notes: Identity assessment: complete three-page primary empirical Short Report, The Face of Success: Inferences From Chief Executive Officers’ Appearance Predict Company Profits, Nicholas O. Rule and Nalini Ambady, Psychological Science, Volume 19 Number 2, pp. 109–111, copyright 2008. Title, authors, journal, year and pages match the neutral reference. DOI is not printed in the supplied text; not independently verifiable within permitted sources. Methods, results, Table 1 and references are present; this is not an abstract or secondary article. No PDF supplied. Target ambiguity: separate power–profits and leadership–profits tests both satisfy the stated three covariates. Power–profits candidate: printed r(41) 5 .36, p < .025. Leadership–profits candidate: printed r(41) 5 .30, p < .05. No combined power-and-leadership predictor is reported. Additional-control tests also appear: profits–leadership controlling for power r(40) 5 .36, p < .025; profits–power controlling for leadership r(40) 5 .40, p < .01. Those have extra controls and do not resolve the locator. No candidate selected using numeric matching or row order. N: 25 highest and 25 lowest companies are initial selection, with exclusions stated separately. No explicit final critical-model analytic N or mutually exclusive final-group counts printed. No N inferred from df or recruitment/exclusion subtraction. Rater counts are contributors, not analytic CEO/company observations. Unassigned replication and reported_success are placeholders only.
